What are reliable yet affordable brands when it comes to used road bikes?

Don't look for a frame brand. You want to look at the groupset branding. Try to buy Shimano.

Frame wise, you want Aluminium at that price range. Shimano Claris is the lowest grade groupset.
Does Shimano assemble them or would it be up the buyer? I've never done it before :p

Well, if you're going to buy a bike second hand you should ride it before you buy it. So it will be assembled.

If you buy it new it will come in a few bits. Pretty easy to put together, but you will need to know how to tune the brakes/gears. You'd have to put the handle bars on, wheels on, seat on, tune the gears/brakes.

Also, you would buy a Trek bike with Shimano gears on it. Shimano just make the gears/brakes.

A good source for bicycle maintenance and repair info is Sheldon Brown: http://sheldonbrown.com/repair/index.html

I am partial to used Trek 800 series bikes for around town. They are heavy. The higher-end bikes are heavily toward Shimano, but none of them is really a bad bike. Put road tires on. Say 26x1.5. Easy miles.

Hold the front brake. Rock the bike back and forth. Feel play? Headset issues. Lift front wheel and turn handlebars. Feel detents? Headset bearings are garbage. Take wheels off. Turn the axle. Should be smooth and w/o play. Spokes kinda tight, no floppy ones. If you can, turn the crank with chain lifted off. Should be smooth. No grinding and no slop. - Check Sheldon for stuff about chain and wear.

Giant and Specialized have a track record of good bikes. Fuji, Peugot, Gitane are also good in older bikes. Look for rust on steel frames. It's usually superficial. But look. Schwinn Collegiate and Varsity are among the decent steel bikes, but not a lot of 'em around these days. Modern Schwinn and GMC are highly questionable.

Cred here is cyclist for more than thirty years. Fella in mid sixties who has ridden a few of this and that over the years. Oh, look at the brands in Wally and elsewhere. Don't buy one of those b/c fixing it will be a problem.

Good luck and good hunting.

Any friends that rides & does maintenance on bicycles themselves? If I were me looking for a used bicycle, I'd ask me to come along to check out the bicycles. It's the same thing as getting a mechanic to look at a automobile before purchasing it from a private party to be notified of all issues with the vehicle. Don't let the seller tell you a problem is "just a little dab of oil to fix".

Also check out your school for a bicycle sale from their impound. UC Irvine has one occasionally and other schools might as well. Speaking of impound, ask with the seller if you can check the frame's serial number (usually located under the bottom bracket area) to check against bike theft (bikeIndex).

If I were to purchase a used road bicycle now.. I'd make sure that critical components are in working order. Critical components to me are things that I can't cheaply replace. Pedals, brake pads, bar tape, and tires & tubes are some things that aren't critical.

frame condition - Make sure there are no visible cracks, deep rust, and it's straight rear cassette & crankset - Make sure the gears aren't worn. races/bearings - Bottom Bracket and the headset. wheel hubs - I honestly don't know how to test this but wheels are expensive. derailures - front and back if there is one.

These should be inspected visually and on the test ride. Bring a notebook with a checklist made... Gosh darn it, I've made it all technical but that's what I would do.

Then again I bought my first road bicycle from bikesdirect, no regrets and I do all my own maintenance. I have seen good/better bicycles from Craigslist for a lower price.

It's not as easy as one thinks, for this reason and also because people don't like shifting to a new dealer if there's nothing wrong with their current guy.
